arxiv-2302-01341.creator: V. Chinnadurai 1 , A. Arulselvam 2 , §
arxiv-2302-01341.description: Abstract . In this paper, we intend the concept of rough cubic Pythagorean fuzzy ideals in the semigroup. By using this notion, we discuss lower approximation and upper approximation of cubic Pythagorean fuzzy left (right) ideals, bi-ideals, interior ideals, and study some of their related properties in detail.

arxiv-2308-07172.title: Economic complexity and the sustainability transition: A review of data, methods, and literature
arxiv-2308-07172.creator: Bernardo Caldarola, Dario Mazzilli, Lorenzo Napolitano, Aurelio Patelli, Angelica Sbardella
arxiv-2308-07172.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bernardo Caldarola, Dario Mazzilli, Lorenzo Napolitano, Aurelio Patelli, Angelica Sbardella. Economic Complexity (EC) methods have gained increasing popularity across fields and disciplines. In particular, the EC toolbox has proved particularly promising in the study of complex and interrelated phenomena, such as the transition towards a greener economy. Using the EC approach, scholars have been investigating the relationship between EC and sustainability, proposing to identify the distinguishing characteristics of green products and to assess the readiness of productive and technological structures for the sustainability transition.

arxiv-2311-08571.creator: Emmanuel Kammerer
arxiv-2311-08571.description: Abstract The purpose of this article is threefold. First, we show that when one explores a conformal loop ensemble of parameter κ = 4 \kappa=4 ( CLE 4 \mathrm{CLE}_{4} ) on an independent 2 2 -Liouville quantum gravity ( 2 2 -LQG) disk, the surfaces which are cut out are independent quantum disks.

arxiv-2402-12179.title: Examining Monitoring System: Detecting Abnormal Behavior In Online Examinations
arxiv-2402-12179.creator: Dinh An Ngo, Thanh Dat Nguyen, Thi Le Chi Dang, Huy Hoan Le, Ton Bao Ho, Vo Thanh Khang Nguyen, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen
arxiv-2402-12179.description: Abstract Cheating in online exams has become a prevalent issue over the past decade, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. To address this issue of academic dishonesty, our “Exam Monitoring System: Detecting Abnormal Behavior in Online Examinations” is designed to assist proctors in identifying unusual student behavior.

arxiv-2406-09650.description: Abstract . The latest trends in the adoption of cloud, edge, and distributed computing, as well as a rise in applying AI/ML workloads, have created a need to measure, monitor, and reduce the carbon emissions of these compute-intensive workloads and the associated communication costs.

arxiv-2407-07147.title: Analytical Insights on Hadronic Top Quark Polarimetry
arxiv-2407-07147.creator: Zhongtian Dong, Dorival Gonçalves, Kyoungchul Kong, Andrew J. Larkoski, Alberto Navarro
arxiv-2407-07147.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhongtian Dong, Dorival Gonçalves, Kyoungchul Kong, Andrew J. Larkoski, Alberto Navarro. Top quark polarization provides an important tool for studying its production mechanisms, spin correlations, top quark properties, and new physics searches. Unlike lighter quarks, the top quark’s polarization remains intact until its decay, enabling precise spin measurements. While the down-type fermions from W W boson decay are known to be effective spin analyzers, charged leptons have typically been the main target for most analyses.

arxiv-2502-00731.title: Diophantine approximation and the subspace theorem
arxiv-2502-00731.creator: Shivani Goel, Rashi Lunia, Anwesh Ray
arxiv-2502-00731.description: Abstract . Diophantine approximation explores how well irrational numbers can be approximated by rationals, with foundational results by Dirichlet, Hurwitz, and Liouville culminating in Roth’s theorem. Schmidt’s subspace theorem extends Roth’s result to higher dimensions, with profound implications for Diophantine equations and transcendence theory.

pmc-10741077.title: Advancements in Understanding and Classifying Chronic Orofacial Pain: Key Insights from Biopsychosocial Models and International Classifications (ICHD-3, ICD-11, ICOP)
pmc-10741077.creator: Federica Canfora, Giulia Ottaviani, Elena Calabria, Giuseppe Pecoraro, Stefania Leuci, Noemi Coppola, Mattia Sansone, Katia Rupel, Matteo Biasotto, Roberto Di Lenarda, Michele Davide Mignogna, Daniela Adamo, Masaru Tanaka, Simone Battaglia
pmc-10741077.description: In exploring chronic orofacial pain (COFP), this review highlights its global impact on life quality and critiques current diagnostic systems, including the ICD-11, ICOP, and ICHD-3, for their limitations in addressing COFP’s complexity. Firstly, this study outlines the global burden of chronic pain and the importance of distinguishing between different pain types for effective treatment.

pmc-11485235.title: The burden of diabetes-associated multiple long-term conditions on years of life spent and lost
pmc-11485235.creator: Edward W Gregg, Adrian Pratt, Alex Owens, Emma Barron, Rupert Dunbar-Rees, Eirion T Slade, Nasrin Hafezparast, Chirag Bakhai, Paul Chappell, Victoria Cornelius, Desmond G Johnston, Jacqueline Mathews, Jason Pickles, Ellie Bragan Turner, Gary Wainman, Kate Roberts, Kamlesh Khunti, Jonathan Valabhji
pmc-11485235.description: Diabetes mellitus is a central driver of multiple long-term conditions (MLTCs), but population-based studies have not clearly characterized the burden across the life course. We estimated the age of onset, years of life spent and loss associated with diabetes-related MLTCs among 46 million English adults.

pmc-11604825.title: Melanoma in people living with HIV: Immune landscape dynamics and the role of immuno- and antiviral therapies
pmc-11604825.creator: Lindsay N Barger, Olivia S El Naggar, Binh Ha, Gabriele Romano
pmc-11604825.description: The intersection of HIV and melanoma presents a complex and unique challenge, marked by distinct patterns in incidence, mortality, and treatment response. Higher mortality rates among people with HIV who develop melanoma underscore an urgent need to identify the factors influencing these outcomes.

pmc-12428404.title: New Frontiers in Cereal and Pseudocereal Germination: Emerging Inducers for Maximizing Bioactive Compounds
pmc-12428404.creator: Hans Himbler Minchán-Velayarce, Atma-Sol Bustos, Luz María Paucar-Menacho, Julio Vidaurre-Ruiz, Marcio Schmiele
pmc-12428404.description: This systematic review analyzes emerging inducers that optimize the germination process of cereals and pseudocereals to enhance bioactive compound production, categorizing them as physical (UV-B radiation, electromagnetic fields, ultrasound, cold plasma), chemical (phytohormones, minerals, growth regulators), and biological (concurrent fermentation, microbial extracts).

pmc-12608017.title: Antiradical and Antioxidant Activity and Stimulation of Pancreatic Lipase by Extracts Obtained from Saponin-Rich Raw Materials: Experimental and In Silico Study
pmc-12608017.creator: Zbigniew Sroka, Karina Kapusta, Klaudia Suchańska, Wojciech Kołodziejczyk, Beata Żbikowska, Andrzej Gamian, Kacper Strzelczyk, Michał Gleńsk, Kamil Wojciechowski, Yakindra Timilsena
pmc-12608017.description: The effects of saponin-rich extracts on pancreatic lipase activity were examined. Horse chestnut seed and ginseng root extracts stimulated lipase activity the most, while ivy leaf and fenugreek seed extracts had an inhibitory effect. The strongest antiradical activity (ABTS+•–2,2-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) test) was exhibited by horse chestnut seed extract and the weakest by the soapwort root extract.

pmc-12635369.title: Mapping hippocampal-cerebellar functional connectivity across the human adult lifespan
pmc-12635369.creator: Kavishini Apasamy, Samuel C. Berry, Marie-Lucie Read, Narender Ramnani, Carl J. Hodgetts
pmc-12635369.description: The hippocampus and cerebellum are traditionally considered to support distinct memory systems, yet evidence from nonhuman species indicates a close relationship during spatial-mnemonic behaviour, with hippocampal projections to and from several cerebellar regions. However, little is known about this relationship in humans.

pmc-12643508.title: IRF7 drives macrophages to kill bacteria and improves septic outcomes via autophagy
pmc-12643508.creator: Guiming Chen, Kangxin Li, Haihua Luo, Lianxu Zhao, Yong Jiang
pmc-12643508.description: Sepsis contributes substantially to mortality rates worldwide, yet clinical trials that have focused on its underlying pathogenesis have failed to demonstrate benefits. Recently, enhancing self-defense has been regarded as an emerging therapeutic approach. Autophagy is a self-defense mechanism that protects septic mice, but its regulatory factor is still unknown.

pmc-12745686.title: Revealing the risk of macroplastic ingestion to marine wildlife
pmc-12745686.creator: Matthew S. Savoca
pmc-12745686.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Sixty years later, the signal has become deafening: roughly 1,500 species consume plastic waste, from zooplankton to whales (5). In some cases, this ingestion proves fatal. Given the intense public and research attention surrounding plastic pollution, it might reasonably be assumed that we know how much plastic is lethal to consume, or how often its ingestion leads to death at a population level. Instead, our knowledge is surprisingly meager. In PNAS, Murphy et al.

pmc-13104527.title: Assessing the potential of urinary dipstick testing to guide empirical antibiotic treatment for urinary tract infections in patients admitted to the emergency department: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13104527.creator: Eugene Yevgeni Feigin, Roy Cohen, Moshe Giladi
pmc-13104527.description: This study of 4,724 bacteriuria cases evaluated if urinary nitrites could guide empiric therapy. Nitrites lacked sensitivity and specificity, failing to accurately distinguish gram-positive from gram-negative pathogens. Because gram-positive infections correlate with age and comorbidities, clinicians should rely on patient characteristics rather than dipstick results to guide empiric antibiotic coverage.
